rationale: Both miss most GT concerns since the shown diff already incorporates the reviewers' fixes (shared _run_varlen_dense helper, FA3 major>=9 gate), so neither can 'recall' issues that no longer exist; both instead surface plausible adjacent issues (duplication, weak FA3 test coverage) that echo the GT's spirit. X's headline, most confidently-stated finding (version=1/2 int args are invalid PEP440 specifiers) is contradicted by the author's own clarification that these are valid branch identifiers, and X also overclaims that the piecewise path crashes on missing varlen_func when that path is actually protected by the None-check in _flash_wrapper. Y is more rigorous: it explicitly validates and rules out the piecewise false lead, and its novel findings (diffusers_adapter match statement silently ignoring the new backend names, GQA/num_kv_heads never checked against the Hq==Hkv kernel requirement, FLASH_ATTN_HUB skipping the compute-capability gate) are concretely grounded with cross-file evidence and file:line citations, giving it materially higher precision and actionability.
